rationale: A search of this app's BSB Matthew finds the noun "cross" first at 10:38 (the word at 8:18 is the verb, "to cross to the other side"), and next at 16:24, where "take up his cross and follow Me" recurs word for word. The saying that follows recurs too: "whoever loses his life for My sake will find it" is identical in 10:39 and 16:25. The noun then returns in the passion narrative itself (27:32, 27:40, 27:42). A recurring phrase tracked through one Gospel is why the type is motif rather than parallel, and the verbatim recurrence is why the label is strong. The Cambridge Bible (on Biblehub) independently notes that at 10:38 "The cross is named for the first time by the Saviour" and that the expression "recurs ch. Matthew 16:24, following upon the announcement of the Passion". Whether Jesus' hearers at 10:38 would already have heard his own death in the words is disputed among the commentators the lesson reports.
